motion.name: player-controls
motion.value: Material 3 AnimatedVisibility with fadeOut() (library default; no custom duration or easing in source)
motion.purpose: Controls appear with the component default and fade after inactivity.

motion.name: translation-panel
motion.value: Modifier.animateContentSize() (Compose default spring; no custom spec)
motion.purpose: Collapsed one-line panel grows to the expanded translation while keeping the page visible.

motion.name: splash-handoff
motion.value: windowSplashScreenAnimationDuration 200 ms plus the existing pop/fade exit helper
motion.purpose: Splash mark hands off to the app without a separate brand animation.

motion.name: drawer-and-sheets
motion.purpose: Navigation surfaces use platform motion; the browser tab sheet changes only its initial expansion state.

evidence.exercise: Phone runtime verified at 1080x2400/density 420, portrait and landscape, font scale 1.0 and 1.3, gesture and three-button navigation.
limits: Manga reader, translation panel and photo viewer reviewed in code only; the live catalogue is adult content.
Russian layout exercised in the player top bar, settings drawer and browser tab sheet; initial broader screen captures are en-US.
No tablet class, security audit or full regression suite claimed.
The rebrand test observed a 16 KB compatibility warning on an earlier build. The 3.7.0 APK passes 64-bit ELF and ZIP alignment checks; these do not test device startup.

components.css: .ds-key { box-sizing: border-box; width: 72px; height: 72px; border-radius: 50%; background: #1C1F24; color: #F4F4F5; border: 1px solid #6F737D; font: 400 28px/36px 'Roboto', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms ease; } .ds-key:hover { background: #23262C; } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #E7A7BE; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-key:active { background: #262A31; }

narrative.overview:
Peachy is an existing native Android media workspace, not a marketing site. The visual system keeps that topology and restyles it through Material 3: full color roles, the standard type scale, the shared shape scale, native navigation and system Back. Depth comes from tonal surfaces, not chrome. Real media stays the loudest thing on every screen; the brand speaks through graphite ground, off-white text, dusty-pink actions and the geometric P lockup rather than through decorative cards, gradients or web landing patterns.

The scheme is dark only and deliberate. Dynamic Color is not used: a wallpaper-derived scheme would replace the brand and can produce light surfaces the app was never verified against. Every role is set explicitly, including containers, inverse pairs and error, so no default Material purple or the previous amber palette survives. The same components serve English and Russian copy; layout is phone-first and must survive a 1.3 font scale, landscape and both gesture and three-button navigation.
keyCharacteristics: Complete explicit Material 3 dark color scheme; no dynamic color and no light theme.
Roboto from the platform, full Material type scale in sp; no bundled display face.
Tonal layering on black/graphite; no drop shadows on app chrome.
Dusty pink reserved for actions, selection, focus and the wordmark period.
Native components and system Back; icon-only or mark-only fallbacks before any clipping.
Black media stages and scrims where honest contrast over video and page art matters.

rules.name: The One Pink Voice Rule
rules.body: primary marks actions, selection and state, and nothing else. Informational section labels use on-surface-variant, body copy uses on-surface or on-background, because a screen where everything is pink has no primary action left.

rules.name: The Hairline Boundary Rule
rules.body: outline-variant draws dividers and nothing interactive. Any control edge — keypad key, outlined button, count badge that needs a border — uses outline so the boundary keeps a perceivable contrast on both the auth card and higher-tonal dialogs.

rules.name: The Dark-Only Rule
rules.body: Do not add a light scheme, dynamicColorScheme, or a per-screen background override. Both platform night mode and the app resolve to the same brand black.

rules.name: The System Face Rule
rules.body: Roboto only. Do not bundle a display font, apply a custom FontFamily, or use letter-spacing as a substitute for hierarchy. Brand voice is color, mark and spacing.

rules.name: The sp Rule
rules.body: Every size, line height and letter spacing stays in sp so the system font-size setting applies. Fixed px text or fixed-height text containers that cannot grow are defects.

rules.name: The Inset Rule
rules.body: The bottom-most interactive content clears navigationBars ∪ mandatorySystemGestures, verified for both navigation modes. Insets are applied once: per surface, never nested a second time.

rules.name: The Back Rule
rules.body: A modal surface consumes Back before the activity does. Predictive-back animation is not claimed as verified; the dismissal contract is.

rules.name: The Tonal-Only Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows on app chrome. If a surface must separate from its background, move it one tonal step or add a 1 dp outline; do not add blur, glow or elevation animation for decoration.

rules.name: The Media Exception Rule
rules.body: Scrims exist only where real media makes contrast unknowable. Do not reuse the black scrim treatment for cards, sheets or dialogs.

rules.name: The Shape-of-the-Theme Rule
rules.body: Use the named shape step that matches the component's role. Do not invent a radius per screen or per state; the only allowed derivative is the translation panel's documented top-only shape.

rules.name: The One Primary Action Rule
rules.body: Each screen or sheet has at most one filled primary action. A second competing action becomes a text or outlined control; a dialog confirmation may be the single primary for that dialog.

rules.name: The Mark-Only Fallback Rule
rules.body: When a slot cannot hold the wordmark, show the mark alone. Never wrap, clip, shrink below the type scale or drop the wordmark's period to make it fit.

dos: Do consume MaterialTheme.colorScheme, MaterialTheme.typography and MaterialTheme.shapes in every screen and keep the explicit palette private to the theme.
Do keep the app dark only, with system bars, splash and window background on the same brand black.
Do give every touch target at least 48 dp and keep the keypad at its 56/72 dp measured sizes.
Do apply window insets once per surface, including mandatorySystemGestures for bottom content on gesture navigation.
Do keep the wordmark on one line via the mark-only fallback and let text grow in sp.
Do keep real media, queue cards and page art unthemed; use black/white scrims only there.
Do describe screens from actual captures and reports, and name what was not exercised.
donts: Don't add Dynamic Color, a light scheme or a wallpaper-derived scheme.
Don't use primary for informational labels, body emphasis or decoration; selection and actions only.
Don't add drop shadows, blur, gradient chrome or custom elevation animation to app surfaces.
Don't hand-pick corner radii or copy raw colors such as Color.DarkGray, Color.Red or platform green/amber into UI chrome.
Don't restyle the player stage, reader, photo viewer or browser fullscreen away from black.
Don't port the website's landing-page composition, marketing cards or hero blocks into the app; native Material topology and system Back come first.
Don't claim the reader, translation panel or Russian locale were runtime-reviewed when the captures do not cover them.
